name: What is a realistic timeline for design and permitting before construction starts?

mainEntity.name: How long should I expect the planning and permit phase to take before the remodel actually begins?
mainEntity.text: How long should I expect the planning and permit phase to take before the remodel actually begins?

acceptedAnswer.text: Before construction starts, a whole-house remodel usually goes through design development, selections, engineering, permit preparation, and city review. That pre-construction phase can be relatively short for a simple update, but it often stretches to several months when the project includes structural changes, custom finishes, or older-home issues. The more decisions that must be made up front, the smoother construction tends to go. Delayed selections can push the project start date because cabinets, windows, tile, and fixtures often need to be ordered before demolition is complete. Complex projects also need more time for plan check and revisions. Homeowners should ask for a separate pre-construction schedule, not just the build schedule. That makes it easier to plan financing, temporary housing, and material ordering. It also reduces frustration when the job has not yet broken ground but still requires active homeowner decisions.
acceptedAnswer.description: The planning phase can take weeks to several months depending on design complexity, engineering needs, and permit review. Projects with structural changes, custom details, or older homes usually need more time before construction can start.
